title: An Empirical Study on Cross-X Transfer for Legal Judgment Prediction

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating legal judgment prediction performance (macro-F1 scores) across different languages (German, French, Italian) to assess the impact of representational disparity, particularly focusing on the performance gap between high-resource and low-resource languages (e.g., Italian) and applying machine translation to mitigate it.

Conducting cross-regional transfer experiments by training and evaluating models on legal cases originating from eight different Swiss regions, assessing how the volume of training cases per region (region-wise representational bias) impacts predictive performance in zero-shot versus in-region evaluations.

Performing cross-domain transfer analysis by fine-tuning models on specific legal areas (e.g., public, civil, penal, social law) and comparing their accuracy to measure how cross-domain representational bias affects outcomes across disparate areas of law.
